purpose: Epicor Kinetic authoritative interface/security evidence promotion.

patch.evidenceNote: Epicor provider documentation establishes versioned, discoverable, OData v4-compliant REST services across Kinetic business objects, processes, reports, BAQs and Epicor Functions, with API keys/access scopes/standard authentication methods and security aligned to ERP user/data permissions. Provider documentation also establishes cloud, on-premises and hybrid Kinetic deployment choices. No sandbox or customer tenant was authenticated and no live read round-trip was performed, so this is specification evidence only.

providerIdentity.regionalHostModel: provider-managed cloud region or customer-managed on-prem/hybrid instance; endpoint is deployment-specific

onPremises.featureReleaseLifecycle: Epicor states 2028.1 is the final on-premises Kinetic feature release, followed by support phases

hybrid.transport: provider cloud plus authorised customer edge for private components

governedReadProjection.note: Epicor documents BAQs as reusable governed data views exposed through REST. Prefer a reviewed BAQ/read projection for WFM extraction when it narrows data and authority versus full business-object/process/function services.

datasetCoverage.absenceMeaning: row may be unchanged, outside the projection/filter/window, hidden by ERP permissions, or outside company/site scope; absence is not deletion
datasetCoverage.entityUniverse: records visible through the exact reviewed projection and constrained integration identity

datasetCoverage.absenceMeaning: candidate absence only after exact company/site/projection scope, every page and reconciliation are proven complete
datasetCoverage.entityUniverse: exact reviewed complete projection for the approved source scope

securityEvidenceBlockers: Epicor states that all Kinetic services, business objects, processes, reports, BAQs and Epicor Functions are accessible through REST. Full service parity therefore includes mutating and executable surfaces; WFM must prove exact read-only service/projection authority and keep processes/functions/actions outside steady-state runtime authority.

Public provider material reviewed establishes API keys, access scopes and standard authentication methods but does not prove the exact customer deployment flow, effective scopes, rotation/revocation behaviour or denied writes. Advance authentication evidence only in an authorised sandbox/tenant with a dedicated least-privilege identity.

BAQs and user-defined fields can expose customer-specific schemas. Exact projection ids, parameters, fields, company/site scope and stable identifiers must be reviewed, fingerprinted and fail closed on breaking drift.

Public provider material reviewed does not establish one universal pagination, delta-token, rate-limit or webhook completeness contract for every Kinetic deployment/service. Discover those contracts from the authorised tenant REST help/metadata and keep bounded polling/reconciliation authoritative until proven.
On-premises/private Kinetic deployments require an authorised customer-edge route. WFM must not scan, bridge or directly expose customer private networks.

Epicor Functions execute custom server-side logic and are excluded from the default connector authority even though they are REST-accessible. Enabling any function/action/write path requires separate explicit approval and proof.
